{
  "need": "Belonging",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "description": "Sitting apart protects against the humiliation of being visibly new and unclaimed; joining risks a public rejection that would confirm they do not matter here." },
  "read": "A mid-year arrival has none of the shared history the room runs on. Every group already has its shape, and stepping toward one uninvited feels like a gamble with dignity. Withdrawing is not shyness so much as a reasonable self-protective move while they read whether this place is safe enough to risk being seen.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Leave them alone and hope they warm up on their own — which feels kind but quietly signals that belonging here is their problem to solve, and the gap widens every day." },
  "mentorMove": "Actively create low-stakes entry points and assign a social bridge before the isolation becomes identity. Hold the standard that everyone is a real member of this class, while giving this student a specific, respected role through which connection can happen naturally.",
  "holdFirm": ["Every student in this room is a full member, not a guest — that standard does not drop because joining feels hard.", "Participation in collaborative work is the expectation for everyone, including students who arrived mid-year."],
  "stayFlexible": ["Let them choose which part of a group task they take on so they can lead from a strength rather than expose a gap.", "Pair them with one well-chosen student first rather than dropping them into a full group, then widen the circle when trust is building."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I wanted to catch you for just a second. Mid-year starts are genuinely hard — the room already has its thing going, and you are figuring out where you fit. That takes time, and I see you working through it." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I ask — is there a subject, a skill, anything you are actually good at or into? Does not have to be school stuff." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I am thinking. I have a spot in this next project where someone who can do that would actually carry the group. I am going to put you with Marcus and Deja — good people, and they need exactly what you bring. You are not being dropped in, you are going in with a job." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to being a real part of this class, not just present in it, because my standard for every person in this room is high and I genuinely think you can do this. I will check in with you after the first session. Deal?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Keep giving this student visible, competence-based roles — note-taker who reports out, the person who teaches a concept to one partner — so belonging arrives through contribution rather than charity, and their status in the room builds on something real."
}
situation: A student who joined mid-year sits apart and has not connected with anyone.
